title: Natural isomorphisms on restricted contravariant pairs after scalar localization
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, C and D preadditive R-linear categories, and t in R. Let q be an object property on C^op times C and q-prime one on the product of the opposite and direct raw scalar localization of C at t. Assume a q-prime pair has underlying integral pair satisfying q. Given integral functors U,V from the full q-subcategory to D and a natural isomorphism alpha:U to V, let F,G be functors from the full q-prime subcategory to the raw scalar localization of D. Suppose their object values are the localized U,V values on the unchanged integral pair. For each pair of objects suppose F.map and G.map on an opposite/direct pair of arrows are separately additive and on pure tensors (x tensor a,y tensor b) equal heterogeneously (xy) tensor U.map(a^op,b), respectively (xy) tensor V.map(a^op,b). Then there is a unique natural isomorphism F to G whose hom and inverse components are heterogeneously the localized hom and inverse of alpha on the integral pair. There are no liftability, faithfulness, triangulatedness or nonzero-ring hypotheses.

proof.text: Conjugate localization.mapIso of each integral alpha component by the prescribed source and target object equalities. The standard equality-transport and heterogeneous-composition lemmas give the required hom and inverse formulas.

For naturality, replace both functor maps by their separately additive actions. Induct first on the opposite-source tensor arrow and then on the direct-target tensor arrow. Zero and sum cases follow from additivity and additive composition. On pure tensors the two composites become integral naturality tensored with the product of the two coefficients, by the scalar-localization composition formula.

Assemble the component isomorphisms using naturality. Any other normalized isomorphism has the same hom components by transitivity of heterogeneous equality, hence equals it by natural-transformation and isomorphism extensionality.

theorem restrictedPairIso_existsUnique
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {C D : Type*}
    [Category* C] [Preadditive C] [Linear R C]
    [Category* D] [Preadditive D] [Linear R D] (t : R)
    (q : ObjectProperty (Cᵒᵖ × C))
    (q' : ObjectProperty ((ScalarLocalization R C t)ᵒᵖ × ScalarLocalization R C t))
    (hq : ∀ P, q' P → q (op P.1.unop.obj, P.2.obj))
    (U V : q.FullSubcategory ⥤ D) (α : U ≅ V)
    (F G : q'.FullSubcategory ⥤ ScalarLocalization R D t)
    (hF : ∀ P, F.obj P = ⟨U.obj ⟨(op P.obj.1.unop.obj, P.obj.2.obj), hq _ P.property⟩⟩)
    (hG : ∀ P, G.obj P = ⟨V.obj ⟨(op P.obj.1.unop.obj, P.obj.2.obj), hq _ P.property⟩⟩)
    (mF : ∀ P Q : q'.FullSubcategory,
      ∃ β : (Q.obj.1.unop ⟶ P.obj.1.unop) →+ (P.obj.2 ⟶ Q.obj.2) →+
          (F.obj P ⟶ F.obj Q),
        (∀ a b, F.map (ObjectProperty.homMk (Prod.mkHom a.op b)) = β a b) ∧
        ∀ a b (x y : Localization.Away t),
          HEq (β (x ⊗ₜ[R] a) (y ⊗ₜ[R] b))
            ((x * y) ⊗ₜ[R] U.map (ObjectProperty.homMk
              (X := ⟨(op P.obj.1.unop.obj, P.obj.2.obj), hq _ P.property⟩)
              (Y := ⟨(op Q.obj.1.unop.obj, Q.obj.2.obj), hq _ Q.property⟩)
              (Prod.mkHom a.op b))))
    (mG : ∀ P Q : q'.FullSubcategory,
      ∃ β : (Q.obj.1.unop ⟶ P.obj.1.unop) →+ (P.obj.2 ⟶ Q.obj.2) →+
          (G.obj P ⟶ G.obj Q),
        (∀ a b, G.map (ObjectProperty.homMk (Prod.mkHom a.op b)) = β a b) ∧
        ∀ a b (x y : Localization.Away t),
          HEq (β (x ⊗ₜ[R] a) (y ⊗ₜ[R] b))
            ((x * y) ⊗ₜ[R] V.map (ObjectProperty.homMk
              (X := ⟨(op P.obj.1.unop.obj, P.obj.2.obj), hq _ P.property⟩)
              (Y := ⟨(op Q.obj.1.unop.obj, Q.obj.2.obj), hq _ Q.property⟩)
              (Prod.mkHom a.op b)))) :
    ∃! e : F ≅ G, ∀ P,
      HEq (e.hom.app P) ((ScalarLocalization.localization R D t).map
        (α.hom.app ⟨(op P.obj.1.unop.obj, P.obj.2.obj), hq _ P.property⟩)) ∧
      HEq (e.inv.app P) ((ScalarLocalization.localization R D t).map
        (α.inv.app ⟨(op P.obj.1.unop.obj, P.obj.2.obj), hq _ P.property⟩))
